kind: Self-review plus independent computational interpretations; no independent agent or human refereeing.
verdict: A concrete small recognizer defeats the single-round strengthening. Full budgeted closure remains open and is not claimed false.

checks.result: The same Phase 3 k and seed radius r are used; all supports and both parity shifts are retained. The new family includes every old noisy input.
Output radius is 2r, not r. A disjoint-error XOR witness tests the necessity of this accounting.
All 16 truth functions are covered; AND/NAND/XOR with recoded primitive inputs generate the same center family. Actual top-gate circuits use at most four ordinary gates.
One operation and shift pair must work on every common-coordinate slice. The code uses OR-of-ANDs in this order, and a regression case distinguishes the wrong order.
Unknown row and column primitive values are independent choices, even for identical address supports; they are not raw outer inputs or free certificates.
2-SAT is expanded into ordinary implication-edge signals, cubic Boolean reachability matrices, and conflict checks.
Exact recognition is claimed only when 2k<m and 2R<2^(m-2k-1). Unsupported parameters are rejected.
The structural check must remain; accepting all augmented 2k-variable functions would not preserve the inner budget.
Reachable gate-ID union/intersection counts preserve real reuse. Allocated unreachable gates and optimal semantic circuit size are not conflated.
For any epsilon>0, choose a small beta_0<1/5 with 2H(beta)<epsilon below it; beta then stays fixed as m grows.
Two composed-center descriptions together use at most 4k coordinates plus parity; fibers give distance at least 2^(m-4k-1), with strict >2R+1 needed for certificates.
A second cheap XOR produces parity on 2k+1 variables, at distance N/2 from every new center. This is a missed YES input, not a NO-soundness failure.
Five new Lean composition/gate-set lemmas and the unchanged old helpers are checked. General 2-SAT/compiler semantics, augmented-feature separation and asymptotics remain manual arguments.
The 64-input network is sampled, not exhaustively evaluated. Its accepted count comes from independently checked center separation and the ball-size formula.

not_established: NP-hardness of the higher-arity structured recognition problem
